```{python}
#| label: fig-continuity
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Continuity test: the tester forces a small current into the pin and measures the resulting voltage across the ESD protection diodes of the DUT. A voltage near one diode drop confirms contact; a voltage running into the limit indicates an open, a near-zero voltage a short."

import schemdraw as sd
import schemdraw.elements as elm

sd.svgconfig.svg2 = False

with sd.Drawing(canvas='svg') as d:
    d.config(unit=2, fontsize=10)

    # tester: current source + voltmeter
    d += elm.SourceI().endpoints((0, 0), (0, 3)).label('$I_\\mathrm{force}$')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0, 3), (3.5, 3))
    d += elm.MeterV().endpoints((2, 3), (2, 0)).label('$V_\\mathrm{meas}$',
                                                      loc='bottom')
    d += elm.Dot().at((2, 3))
    d += elm.Dot().at((1, 0))

    # pin boundary
    d += elm.Dot(open=True).at((3.5, 3)).label('pin', 'top')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((3.5, 3), (6, 3))

    # DUT ESD diodes
    d += elm.Diode().endpoints((6, 3), (6, 5)).label('$D_1$', loc='bottom')
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((6, 5), (6, 5.5))
    d += elm.Vdd().at((6, 5.5)).label('$V_\\mathrm{DD}$')
    d += elm.Diode().endpoints((6, 0.5), (6, 3)).label('$D_2$',
                                                       loc='bottom')
    d += elm.Dot().at((6, 3))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((6, 0.5), (6, 0))
    d += elm.Ground().at((6, 0))
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((6, 3), (7.5, 3))
    d += elm.Gap().endpoints((7.5, 3), (8.5, 3)).label('to core')

    # ground return of tester
    d += elm.Line().endpoints((0, 0), (2, 0))
    d += elm.Ground().at((1, 0))
```
